transcript.text: My indesit washing machine fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all. Its an IWC something. Had it about 9 years. Is it worth fixing?

It depends on what the fault turns out to be. If it is the drive belt, that is usually a simple, low-cost repair and generally worth doing even on a 9-year-old machine. From what you have described, the most likely cause is drive belt [belt-driven machines ONLY]. Check how the drum moves by hand. With the machine unplugged and the door open, how does the drum feel when you turn it by hand — normal, much lighter or looser than usual, or stiff, rough or grinding?
I've turned it by hand with the power off and it turns freely and quietly, no scraping or rumbling. It feels normal to me.
Let's see whether the machine itself can spin: take the washing out and run a spin-only programme with the drum empty. Does it spin up properly when it's empty?
I ran it empty as you suggested and the drum doesn't turn at all in spin either. It fills, drains and the door locks, but there's no rotation. Occasionally a light flashes after a long wait.

With the machine unplugged and the door open, push the drum firmly down and lift it up, then rock it side to side. Does the drum feel loose — dropping, knocking or clunking — or firm with just a slight springy movement?

I'm not sure I can judge that very well, as I haven't got a reference for what's normal. There's no obvious clunking or knocking that I can tell, but I haven't tried it yet in a careful way. Is this check likely to tell us much, given the drum turns freely by hand?

Not much more. A drum that turns freely and quietly by hand rules out a jam or rough bearings, but it can't show whether the machine is actually trying to turn the drum, so that's the part still to narrow down. It's also worth checking the settings: wool, delicate and hand-wash programmes spin very gently, and options such as "no spin", "rinse hold" or a low spin speed stop the final spin. Was a normal programme with a normal spin speed selected, or was one of those options set?

I can't say I remember which settings I used, but I believe it was a normal cotton wash with the usual spin speed, and I didn't select any no-spin or rinse hold option. The drum didn't turn in the wash part either, not just the spin. Also, I once noticed a faint hot electrical smell a few weeks ago, though not since.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
